name: Ajar (PoC C)
description: Ajar — per-video YouTube approvals. Policy-installed; enforces the shared policy model with full-URL blocking webRequest.
//policy_install_note: webRequestBlocking is honored ONLY because this extension is force-installed by enterprise policy (ExtensionInstallForcelist). Chrome's MV3 migration guide states policy-installed extensions keep the blocking form of webRequest: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/develop/migrate/blocking-web-requests . A store-installed MV3 extension could not use webRequestBlocking and would be limited to declarativeNetRequest. See windows/extension/README.md.
//options_note: Dev/browser-testable enrollment: point the extension at the backend and redeem a one-time code. In production on Windows the LocalSystem service is the policy source and this page is unnecessary.

//permissions_note.tabs: Re-check already-open tabs when policy changes: reopen a page the parent has just approved, and catch anything the MV3 cold-start window let slip.
//permissions_note.webRequest: Observe network requests (URLs) to evaluate against policy.
//permissions_note.webRequestBlocking: Synchronous onBeforeRequest so we can cancel/redirect a disallowed navigation BEFORE it loads. Available because policy-installed (see policy_install_note). This is the per-URL decision path.
//permissions_note.declarativeNetRequest: Static/dynamic rules for coarse host-level blocks (e.g. unsupported YouTube-adjacent hosts) that don't need per-request JS. Complements, does not replace, the blocking webRequest per-video path. DNR dynamic-rule limits: 30,000 rules total, 5,000 'unsafe' (redirect/modifyHeaders) — https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/declarativeNetRequest .
//permissions_note.webNavigation: Catch YouTube SPA route changes (onHistoryStateUpdated) where the video changes via history.pushState with no full document navigation — these never hit onBeforeRequest as a top-level nav.
//permissions_note.storage: Cache the last signed policy snapshot pushed from the native host so evaluation works between native-host round-trips.
//permissions_note.nativeMessaging: Connect to the LocalSystem service's native-messaging host to receive signed policy snapshots and to post AccessRequests from the block page.

//host_permissions_note: YouTube hosts are listed explicitly because YouTube is the first-class content type this PoC gates per-video (watch pages, shorts, embeds, short links, nocookie, kids) plus the playback-support hosts an approved video needs. <all_urls> is REQUIRED and justified: the shared policy model is not YouTube-only — it evaluates DOMAIN / URL / URL_PATTERN / CATEGORY rules and supports a default-deny web posture (DefaultPolicy.webDefault in shared/policy/policy-model.ts). To enforce exact-URL and domain rules on arbitrary sites, and to run onBeforeRequest across all navigations, the extension must observe all URLs. It inspects URLs to make allow/block decisions; it does not exfiltrate browsing history (privacy posture: ARCHITECTURE.md §10).
//web_accessible_resources_note: blocked.html must be web-accessible so onBeforeRequest can redirect a blocked navigation to chrome-extension://<id>/blocked.html?u=<enc>. Redirect to a web_accessible_resource extension page is supported for blocked navigations.
